prompt: How are the two rings of decalin joined?

choices.text: Two cyclohexane rings share two carbon atoms and the bond between them
Two cyclohexane rings are connected by a single bond between one carbon of each
choices.why: Decalin's rings are fused: they share a common bond, so two carbons belong to both rings.

choices.text: Two cyclohexane rings share a single carbon atom
choices.why: Decalin's rings share two carbons, the bridgehead carbons C1 and C6, plus the bond joining them.

choices.text: A cyclohexane ring and a cyclopentane ring share one bond
choices.why: Both of decalin's rings are six-membered. A five-membered ring fused to six-membered ones appears in steroids.

explanation: Decalin consists of two cyclohexane rings joined to share two carbon atoms (the bridgehead carbons, C1 and C6) and a common bond. Rings fused together along a common bond make a polycyclic molecule.

prompt: Decalin is made of two six-membered rings that share two carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms does decalin have?
explanation: Two cyclohexane rings have 6 + 6 = 12 ring positions, but the two bridgehead carbons (C1 and C6) belong to both rings, so decalin has 12 − 2 = 10 carbons.

prompt: In decalin, what are the bridgehead carbons?

choices.text: The two carbons, C1 and C6, shared by both rings
The carbons that carry axial hydrogens
choices.why: Every ring carbon in a chair has an axial position. Bridgeheads are defined by being shared between the rings.

choices.text: The carbons farthest from the ring fusion
choices.why: The bridgeheads are at the fusion itself: they are the two carbons common to both rings.

choices.text: All ten carbons, since each is part of a ring
choices.why: Only the two carbons that belong to both rings, C1 and C6, are bridgeheads.

explanation: Decalin consists of two cyclohexane rings joined to share two carbon atoms, the bridgehead carbons C1 and C6, and a common bond.

choices.text: In cis-decalin the bridgehead hydrogens are on the same side of the rings; in trans-decalin they are on opposite sides
In cis-decalin both rings are chairs; in trans-decalin one ring is a boat
choices.why: Both isomers can be represented with chair cyclohexane rings (Figure 4.9.1). The difference is where the bridgehead hydrogens point.

choices.text: Cis-decalin has its rings sharing one bond; trans-decalin's rings share two
choices.why: Both isomers have two cyclohexane rings sharing the same two carbons and one common bond.

choices.text: Cis-decalin has two six-membered rings; trans-decalin has one six- and one five-membered ring
choices.why: Both isomers are two cyclohexane rings. Cis and trans refer to the faces of the rings the bridgehead hydrogens are on.

explanation: In cis-decalin, the hydrogen atoms at the bridgehead carbons are on the same side of the rings; in trans-decalin, the bridgehead hydrogens are on opposite sides (Figure 4.9.1).

prompt: Can cis-decalin be converted into trans-decalin by a ring-flip?

choices.text: No; they are cis–trans stereoisomers and are not interconvertible by ring-flips or other rotations
Yes; a ring-flip of either ring converts cis to trans
choices.why: A ring-flip changes axial and equatorial positions, not which face of the ring a group is on, so cis stays cis.

choices.text: Yes; they are two conformations of the same molecule
choices.why: Conformations interconvert by rotation around single bonds. The decalins are different compounds (stereoisomers).

choices.text: Only at high temperature, when ring-flipping becomes fast enough
choices.why: No amount of ring-flipping interconverts them; it would require breaking bonds.

explanation: The two decalin isomers are not interconvertible by ring-flips or other rotations. They are cis–trans stereoisomers.

prompt: The relationship between cis- and trans-decalin is the same as the relationship between which pair?

choices.text: cis- and trans-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane
The axial and equatorial conformations of methylcyclohexane
choices.why: Those are conformations that interconvert by a ring-flip. The decalins are stereoisomers that can't.

choices.text: The anti and gauche conformations of butane
choices.why: Those interconvert by rotation around a single bond; cis- and trans-decalin do not.

choices.text: The chair and boat conformations of cyclohexane
choices.why: Chair and boat are conformations of one molecule; cis- and trans-decalin are different compounds.

explanation: Cis- and trans-decalin are cis–trans stereoisomers and have the same relationship to each other that cis- and trans-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane have.

prompt: What ring system do steroids such as testosterone have?

choices.text: Three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring fused together
Two six-membered rings fused together
choices.why: That is decalin. Steroids have four fused rings.

choices.text: Four six-membered rings fused together
choices.why: One of the four rings in a steroid is five-membered.

choices.text: A boat cyclohexane ring bridged by a CH2 group
choices.why: That describes norbornane, bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane.

explanation: Steroids, such as testosterone, the primary sex hormone in males, have three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring fused together.

prompt: How well do the principles of cyclohexane conformational analysis apply to steroids?

choices.text: They apply equally well, and often better, than to simple cyclohexanes
They don't apply; fused rings need entirely different rules
choices.why: The same principles that apply to simple cyclohexane rings apply to steroids.

choices.text: They apply only to the five-membered ring
choices.why: Chair-conformation analysis is about six-membered rings, and steroids have three of them.

choices.text: They apply only after the rings are broken open into an acyclic chain
choices.why: The analysis applies directly to the fused rings; no ring has to be opened.

explanation: Although steroids look complicated compared with cyclohexane or decalin, the same principles that apply to the conformational analysis of simple cyclohexane rings apply equally well (and often better) to steroids.

prompt: Why are decalin and norbornane called bicycloalkanes?

choices.text: Two rings would have to be broken open to generate an acyclic structure
Each has exactly two carbon atoms in a ring
choices.why: Bicyclo refers to the number of rings, not carbons: decalin has 10 ring carbons and norbornane 7.

choices.text: Each has two bridges connecting the bridgehead carbons
choices.why: Norbornane has three bridges (2, 2 and 1 carbons). Bicyclo counts rings, defined by how many must be broken to give a chain.

choices.text: Each has two double bonds
choices.why: Both are alkanes, with only single bonds.

explanation: Like decalin, norbornane is a bicycloalkane, so called because two rings would have to be broken open to generate an acyclic structure.

prompt: How many carbon atoms does norbornane, bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane, have?
explanation: The systematic name bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane says the molecule has seven carbons: two bridgehead carbons connected by bridges of 2, 2 and 1 carbon atoms (2 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 7).

prompt: In the name bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane, what do the numbers in brackets mean?

choices.text: Three bridges, of 2, 2 and 1 carbon atoms, connect the two bridgehead carbons
Substituents are on carbons 2, 2 and 1
choices.why: Norbornane is unsubstituted. The bracketed numbers count the carbons in each bridge.

choices.text: The molecule has rings of 2, 2 and 1 carbons
choices.why: No ring can have one or two carbons. The numbers count bridge carbons between the bridgeheads.

choices.text: The bridgeheads are carbons 2, 2 and 1
choices.why: There are two bridgehead carbons; the three numbers describe the bridges joining them.

explanation: The systematic name bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane reflects the fact that the molecule has seven carbons, is bicyclic, and has three "bridges" of 2, 2, and 1 carbon atoms connecting the two bridgehead carbons.

prompt: Which description of norbornane's shape is correct?

choices.text: A conformationally locked boat cyclohexane in which carbons 1 and 4 are joined by an extra CH2 group
A chair cyclohexane that ring-flips rapidly, with a CH2 bridge across it
choices.why: The one-carbon bridge between C1 and C4 holds the six-membered ring as a boat; it can't flip to a chair.

choices.text: Two cyclohexane chairs fused along a common bond
choices.why: That is decalin. Norbornane has seven carbons, not ten.

choices.text: A flat cyclohexane ring with a CH2 group above it
choices.why: The six-membered ring is a boat, not flat; a model helps show its three-dimensional shape.

explanation: Norbornane has a conformationally locked boat cyclohexane ring (Section 4.5) in which carbons 1 and 4 are joined by an additional CH2 group.

prompt: In the usual drawing of norbornane, what does a break in the rear bond indicate?

choices.text: The vertical bond crosses in front of it
The rear bond is missing, so the ring is open there
choices.why: Norbornane has all its bonds; the break is a drawing convention for one bond passing in front of another.

choices.text: The rear bond is a double bond
choices.why: Norbornane is an alkane. The break shows which bond is in front, not bond order.

choices.text: The rear bond is longer than the others
choices.why: The break only shows depth: the vertical bond passes in front of it.

explanation: In drawing norbornane, a break in the rear bond indicates that the vertical bond crosses in front of it. Making a molecular model is particularly helpful for seeing its three-dimensionality.

prompt: Camphor, found in nature, is an example of which kind of compound?

choices.text: A substituted norbornane
A steroid
choices.why: Steroids have three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring fused together; camphor is built on the bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane skeleton.

choices.text: A substituted decalin
choices.why: Decalin is two fused six-membered rings; camphor's skeleton is the bridged norbornane system.

choices.text: A monosubstituted cyclohexane
choices.why: Camphor is bicyclic, based on norbornane.

explanation: Substituted norbornanes, such as camphor, are found widely in nature, and many have been important historically in developing organic structural theories.
